label: verify-bm-bilayer-theory-verified

claims.claim: Project f(m,n) is Timoshenko's eq.(4) (also R&M, FFC with E->E/(1-nu)); narrow-strip assumptions; Timoshenko 1925 does not state the ceiling 3/2 or optimum m^2n=1; identity 3/2 - f = 3(m^2n-1)^2/(2(...)).
claims.source_says: the following general equation for the curvature of a bi-metal strip will be obtained, 1/p = 6(a2-a1)(t-t0)(1+m)^2 / h(3(1+m)^2+(1+mn)(m^2+1/(mn))). Search of pp.233-242 text found no 'optimum'/'best'.
claims.note: Eq.(4) reads as stated and the identity reproduces numerically; I searched only PDF pages 41-51 for optimum, and did not open R&M's equation images or the FFC preprint.

claims.claim: For a wide plate Timoshenko substitutes E/(1-nu), f unchanged (sphere, sag < h/2); beyond bifurcation curvature is (1+nu) times strip value (cylinder), D_c about 4.2 sqrt(h/kappa); strip safe below about 2 sqrt(h/kappa).
claims.source_says: substitute E/(1-sigma) instead of E1 and E2... equations (4) and (6) remain without any change... If the deflections are small, say less than a half of the thickness of the plate... Pezzulla: The minimization gives L + N = kappa_o(1 + nu) and K = 0
claims.note: Timoshenko and Pezzulla (1+nu) statements check out; the 4.2 and 2.0 sqrt(h/kappa) boundaries are the agent's own derived numbers, and Alben's model and sympy derivation were not re-run.

claims.claim: Diffusion-limited actuation tau ~ h^2/D (R&M) with sub-quadratic fits 1.3-1.5; D of printable polymers 0.001-0.0151 mm^2/h; 90% curvature response at 0.72 a^2/D gives 1.9-29 h (0.2 mm), 7.7-116 h (0.4), 31-463 h (0.8); no Formlabs D found.
claims.source_says: For molecular pores, D ~ 10^-9 m2/s, h_a ~ 1 mm and tau = h_a^2/D ~ 1000 s... shrinking time varies as 96 h_a^1.5 min and swelling time as 29 h_a^1.3 min. Table: Nylon 0.001, PLA T-W 0.0151 mm2/h.
claims.note: R&M and Aniskevich values match, and the agent's script rerun gives t90=0.7239 a^2/D, so the real-unit times reproduce; 'no Formlabs D' is an absence claim I could not prove.

claims.claim: Armon 2011, Alben-Balakrisnan-Smela 2011 and Freund 2000 could not be read in the original; only abstracts or a companion paper, so statements about them are second-hand.
claims.source_says: Europe PMC abstract of Armon 2011: we modeled the pod as a thin strip with a flat intrinsic metric and a saddle-like intrinsic curvature.
claims.note: The Armon abstract quote matches; the claim concerns the agent's own access limits, which I only partly confirmed (Armon abstract only, others not fetched).

overall: The four key claims largely hold. Timoshenko eq.(4), the plate substitution and the sag < h/2 limit, the R&M and Aniskevich numbers, the Pezzulla (1+nu) result and the 3/2 identity all reproduce. The strip/plate boundary values (2.0 and 4.2 sqrt(h/kappa)) are the agent's own derivations. I did not re-check Alben's model, the FFC preprint, or R&M's equation images.
